Attackers supplied transaction references without corresponding records. The November update, CIAD-2026-0058, reports modified applications defeating assumptions that only legitimate clients would call APIs, and explicitly recommends approval controls for merchant settlements.

My verification question is: what prevents execution when business approval is absent?

Ask payment engineering and finance control owners to trace one disbursement and one merchant settlement path together. In an authorized test environment, check that valid credentials cannot enable execution without an approved record, without preceding validation, or above applicable limits. Record where rejection occurs, then extend the review to every fund-movement path.

request.task: You are a strict LinkedIn publish-quality evaluator. Score the finished post, not the raw topic, from 0 (absent) to 5 (exceptional) on each named dimension. Judge whether the post is understandable, useful, specific, distinctive, interesting, shareable, and authentic enough to publish. Do not reward clickbait, engagement bait, unsupported specificity, or generic LinkedIn polish. Use the supplied evidence only to judge whether concrete details are grounded. This is a publish-readiness heuristic, not a promise of virality. These ratings are not calibrated to the author's human judgments or engagement outcomes. Apply the rating anchors to each dimension; never inflate scores to meet a threshold. Use the same brief and voice context as the writer. If writing_voice is present, assess voice fit against its selected style_traits over default persona style; approved examples supply compatible details only. Preserve factual and author-POV boundaries. Identify the largest fixable defect first; missing factual support is an evidence-brief gap, not permission to invent a better story. Return JSON only.
